messages:
Sara Chen: Heads-up — AcmeCorp just escalated. On Dedicated cluster 'acme-west-1' they're seeing prolonged 429s and requests timing out. They say autoscaling didn't add replicas fast enough during the spike.
Jon Patel: Ugh. Any repro steps or logs from them?
Sara Chen: From Acme support: burst from their side ~300->900 concurrent requests over ~30s; our api returned 429s for ~90s. They noted min_replicas=2, max_replicas=30 in their config. They included this header from a failing request: `x-rw-error: capacity_throttle`.
Maria Gomez (Acct): Customer is pretty upset — they started a paid Dedicated contract last month. Need ETA on fix / workaround ASAP.
Lee Nguyen: tagging oncall — @Vikram Rao can you take a look? Suspect cold starts + our provision window. :eyes:
Vikram Rao: on it. Do we have autoscaler logs for that cluster window? Also need to confirm whether nodes were available in the pool or we queued on cloud provider.
infra-bot: autoscaler.event: timestamp=2026-02-22T15:03:12Z cluster=acme-west-1 action=scale_check current_replicas=2 pending_scale_up=0 recommended=9 reason="queue_length_high"
infra-bot: cloud.provision: timestamp=2026-02-22T15:03:18Z request_id=prov-9ab3 status=queued provider_wait_time=22s
Vikram Rao: looks like provisioning was queued by cloud provider for ~20s. That + container coldstart could cause the observed 90s window. Any throttles in our front proxy while waiting?
Jon Patel: Checking edge proxy logs — we have short-term 429 surge protection when backend concurrency exceeded 250. That can amplify customer errors. We should surface better 429 reason codes.
Sara Chen: Customer also reported a few 500s with message `backend_unavailable`.
Lee Nguyen: Can you paste the autoscaler policy (snippet) from their tenant config?
Sara Chen: They run:
```
min_replicas: 2
max_replicas: 30
scale_policy:
  metric: queue_length
  threshold: 50
  step_up: 3
  cooldown: 30s
```
Vikram Rao: Step_up=3 + cooldown 30s explains slow ramp when burst is >300 reqs. Also provider queue added ~20s per batch of nodes. Two mitigations: temporarily increase min_replicas to 8 or enable warm pool on the Dedicated profile.
Maria Gomez (Acct): Can we propose a temporary config to the customer and schedule a follow-up? They want immediate relief.
Jon Patel: For immediate relief I suggest: bump min_replicas to 8, reduce cooldown to 10s, and enable fast-provisioning zone if available. I'll open a deploy change for the tenant config and coordinate with infra to request faster node allocation.
Vikram Rao: I'll also add proxy exception to avoid 429 surge-protection for this tenant for the next hour while nodes come up. Note: we need a rollback plan if noise occurs.
Sara Chen: Repro steps from support to validate once changes applied:
1) Run 10s warmup: `hey -c 200 -q 50 -z 60s https://dedicated.acme.redwood/v1/generate`
2) Then spike: `hey -c 900 -q 200 -z 30s` and watch `x-rw-error` and 429 rate.
Support Bot: Created ticket RW-8762 and linked customer report.
Jon Patel: Change pushed to staging tenant config. Will push to prod in 2 mins and post update.
(5 minutes pass)
Jon Patel: Prod change applied: min_replicas=8, cooldown=10s, warm_pool=true for acme-west-1. Rolling update started.
infra-bot: cloud.provision: timestamp=2026-02-22T15:11:40Z request_id=prov-9ab3 status=allocating nodes_allocated=6
Vikram Rao: Disabled surge 429 rule for acme tenant temporarily.
Sara Chen: Re-ran repro (support): initial warmup then spike — customer reports 429s dropped to <1% and median latency back to ~400ms. They saw one 500 during provisioning but overall good.
Maria Gomez (Acct): Customer on call is pleased and asks for post-mortem and two things: (1) documented mitigation steps, (2) proposal for SLAs around scale-up time.
Lee Nguyen: Agreed — I'll own a short postmortem and proposed fixes: warm pools for Dedicated by default, faster default cooldown for queue-based policies, expose clearer throttle reason codes, and a provider-side provisioning SLA.
Vikram Rao: Also adding autoscaler metric: `time_to_target_replicas` to track scale latency per tenant. I'll instrument and create alert if median > 60s.
Sara Chen: Great — I'll update the customer and close the immediate escalation. Thanks all. :tada:
Jon Patel: Follow-up actions in RW-8762. Leaving this thread open for the postmortem draft.
Maria Gomez (Acct): Thanks team — marking as high priority for PM review.
